cases.name: Denise Roach
cases.narrative:
On 5/28/1996, her body was found in a pond on the property where he was employed as a landscaper. According to the medical examiner, her body was very decomposed and had probably been in the water for seven to ten days. She had 16 puncture wounds to her skull, fractures to her face and skull and injuries consistent with manual strangulation.

The medical examiner also noted two large slits in Roach’s clothing caused by a sharp instrument, and determined that Roach died from the combination of strangulation, puncture wounds and blunt trauma to the head.

Friends and family portrayed Smithers as a deeply religious man who lived quietly in the Walden Lake subdivision.

But prosecutors said there was a dark side to Smithers. They said he drove his pickup truck to a Hillsborough Avenue motel, picked up 24-year-old Roach and took her to Whitehurst's unoccupied property near Plant City. There, he smashed her in the face, choked her and stabbed her repeatedly in the skull with a sharp weapon.
